example.answer: The annual salary is $52,000, the weekly pay is $1,000, and the average monthly pay is $4,333.33.
example.problem: You earn $25 per hour and work 40 hours a week. What is that as an annual salary?
example.title: From $25 an hour to a yearly salary

faqs.a: Multiply the hourly wage by hours worked per week, then by 52 weeks. For example, $25 × 40 × 52 = $52,000 per year.
faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly wage to a salary?

faqs.a: Divide the salary by 52 to get weekly pay, then divide by hours worked per week. A $60,000 salary at 40 hours a week is $60,000 ÷ 52 ÷ 40 ≈ $28.85 per hour.
faqs.q: How do I convert a salary to an hourly wage?

faqs.a: It assumes you work every week of the year with no unpaid time off. If you take 2 unpaid weeks, multiply by 50 instead of 52.
faqs.q: Does this account for unpaid vacation?

faqs.a: No. These are gross figures before tax. Your take-home pay depends on income tax, social security, and any deductions in your country or state.
faqs.q: Is this before or after tax?

formula.expr: annual salary = hourly wage × hours per week × 52
formula.label: Hourly to annual

formula.expr: hourly wage = annual salary ÷ 52 ÷ hours per week
formula.label: Annual to hourly

howItWorks: Converting between hourly and annual pay is a simple chain of multiplications. To go from hourly to annual, multiply the wage by the hours you work each week to get weekly pay, then multiply by 52 weeks to get the yearly figure. To go the other way, divide the annual salary by 52 to get weekly pay, then divide by your weekly hours to land on the hourly rate. The calculator also shows the average monthly pay, which is the annual figure divided by 12.

These are gross estimates for planning purposes, not financial advice. They assume a full 52 working weeks with no unpaid leave, and they are before tax — your take-home pay will be lower after income tax and deductions.

When you compare two offers, convert both to the same unit before deciding. A $52,000 salary at 40 hours a week beats a $55,000 salary at 50 hours a week once you divide by the hours: the first is $25.00 an hour and the second is only about $21.15. Overtime rules, bonuses, and benefits also change the real comparison, so use the hourly rate as your starting point and layer those on top.
intro: Convert an hourly wage to an annual salary, or an annual salary back to an hourly rate. Enter your pay and hours per week to compare job offers, negotiate a raise, or see what that hourly rate really means per year.

mistakes.text: A $52,000 salary is not $52,000 in your pocket. Income tax and deductions come out first, so compare gross with gross and net with net.
mistakes.title: Comparing before-tax and after-tax numbers

mistakes.text: If you take unpaid time off, 52 weeks overstates your pay. With 2 unpaid weeks, a $25 hourly wage at 40 hours is $50,000, not $52,000.
mistakes.title: Forgetting unpaid time off

mistakes.text: A $55,000 salary at 50 hours a week is about $21.15 per hour — less than a $50,000 salary at 40 hours ($24.04). Always divide by your actual hours.
mistakes.title: Ignoring the hours behind a salary

mistakes.text: Monthly pay is the annual salary divided by 12, an average. Some months you receive two paychecks and some three if you are paid biweekly.
mistakes.title: Treating monthly pay as exact
